meta.unit: Voyage to the promised land (1 Nephi 16–18)

world_behind.title: The route runs down the incense trail
world_behind.text: "Nearly a south-southeast direction" (v. 13) from the Red Sea camp tracks the ancient caravan road along Arabia's western mountains: watered stations, hunting country, and established stopping places. The record's directional notes are the kind a traveler keeps.

cites.quote: Nearly a south-southeast direction

spans.text: Nearly a south-southeast direction

world_behind.title: Nahom was somebody's place already
world_behind.text: Ishmael "was buried in the place which was called Nahom" (v. 34): called, not named by the family. The wording is the claim. Shazer they "did call" (v. 13); Nahom "was called". The travelers arrive at an existing name in somebody's country. An ancient tribal region with a name of just that shape is attested by inscription in south Arabia, on this very corridor, among the record's most checkable geographical claims. Readers have also long noted the fit of sound and scene: the name recalls Hebrew words for mourning and comfort, and the family stops there to grieve.

cites.quote: was buried in the place which was called Nahom

spans.text: was buried in the place which was called Nahom

cites.quote: did call

spans.text: did call

world_behind.title: A steel-fitted bow was elite equipment
world_behind.text: "My bow, which was made of fine steel" (v. 18) describes a prized composite weapon, the best hunting technology a wealthy Jerusalem house could carry. Its breaking, with the other bows' "having lost their springs" (v. 21) (resin and sinew fail in humid coastal air), disarmed the whole camp at once; the crisis was technological before it was spiritual.

cites.quote: My bow, which was made of fine steel

spans.text: My bow, which was made of fine steel

cites.quote: having lost their springs

spans.text: having lost their springs

world_behind.title: Hunting fed the caravan
world_behind.text: Bows, arrows, slings, and stones (v. 15) are a desert hunter's full kit; game along the fertile fringes was the company's protein. A camp that cannot hunt starves in weeks. That fact sits underneath the murmuring of verses 19–20.

world_behind.title: The ball arrives unexplained
world_behind.text: "A round ball of curious workmanship" (v. 10) of fine brass, found at the tent door, never named in this book; the record calls it "the ball" for five hundred pages until Alma supplies "Liahona" (Alma 37:38). Israel had been led before, by cloud and fire (Ex. 13:21); this instrument is more intimate: handheld, legible, and tuned to the household's conduct.

cites.quote: A round ball of curious workmanship

spans.text: A round ball of curious workmanship

world_behind.title: Burials bound families to places
world_behind.text: Interring Ishmael at a named site along the trail follows the age's practice: graves belonged to places, and places to memory. His daughters' mourning (v. 35) is also a grievance list, and the record preserves both: real grief, and the accusation it fed.

words.text: A courtroom word, and Nephi uses it of his own preaching: "the righteous have I justified" (v. 2). To justify is to declare a person in the right, a verdict rather than a compliment. The same sermon that cuts one set of hearers clears another, and Nephi answers the charge of speaking hard things by pointing at both results. The record will use the word only once more, and then of the law that cannot do it (2 Ne. 2:5).

cites.quote: the righteous have I justified

spans.text: the righteous have I justified

words.text: Old English for carefully made (full of care, wrought with skill), not odd. The ball is "of curious workmanship" (v. 10), and the word places it in the record's running line of appraised craft: Laban's sword, the ship to come, the temple after. Nephi notices work, and heaven's work most of all.

cites.quote: of curious workmanship

spans.text: of curious workmanship

words.text: The bows "having lost their springs" (v. 21) is archer's language: a bow's spring is its stored power, and desert heat and coastal damp kill it. One word carries the whole camp's predicament: equipment mortality in a place where equipment is life.

cites.quote: having lost their springs

spans.text: having lost their springs

words.text: "I did say many things unto them in the energy of my soul" (v. 24). Energy is force put out, the whole of a man spent on his words, and it is a word the Bible never uses. Nephi had reached for its plural the chapter before, exhorting his brothers with all the energies of his soul (1 Ne. 15:25). Both times the word measures how much of himself went into the saying.

cites.quote: I did say many things unto them in the energy of my soul

spans.text: I did say many things unto them in the energy of my soul

words.text: Correction from love, and no one is exempt: Lehi "was truly chastened because of his murmuring" (v. 25), and the company later "were chastened by the voice of the Lord" (v. 39). The record's discipline vocabulary makes its debut on the prophet himself. That is what makes it bearable when it lands on everyone else.

cites.quote: was truly chastened because of his murmuring

spans.text: was truly chastened because of his murmuring

cites.quote: were chastened by the voice of the Lord

spans.text: were chastened by the voice of the Lord

words.text: In older English cunning means skill: the tabernacle's fine work was done by cunning workmen (Ex. 31:4). Laman keeps the skill and adds the malice, telling the others that Nephi "worketh many things by his cunning arts, that he may deceive our eyes" (v. 38). The accusation grants his brother real ability and denies him any source for it but himself.

cites.quote: worketh many things by his cunning arts, that he may deceive our eyes

spans.text: worketh many things by his cunning arts, that he may deceive our eyes

phrases.term: The guilty taketh the truth to be hard
phrases.text: The record's proverb about its own reception, minted in the tent: truth "cutteth them to the very center" (v. 2). Hardness, the proverb says, is a symptom to be read backward; the cut locates the wound. Jacob will preach its twin a generation on (2 Ne. 9:40), and every hard chapter of the record leans on it.

cites.quote: cutteth them to the very center

spans.text: cutteth them to the very center

phrases.term: A round ball of curious workmanship
phrases.text: The instrument arrives without instructions, explanation, or name, found at the door, pointing the way. The record keeps it strange on purpose: guidance in this family is a given thing, working by rules the travelers must discover through use, and its name will wait five hundred pages for a teaching moment (Alma 37:38).

The ball's routing policy in four words: not manna, not shortcuts: "the more fertile parts of the wilderness" (v. 16). Guidance optimizes within hardship; the wilderness stays wilderness, and the Lord's leading shows in which wilderness. It is the record's most realistic sentence about being led.

cites.quote: the more fertile parts of the wilderness

spans.text: the more fertile parts of the wilderness

phrases.text: The new bow is Nephi's; the question is his father's. Having just out-performed every adult in the camp, Nephi routes the decision through the humbled patriarch, "Whither shall I go to obtain food" (v. 23), and the question itself restores the order murmuring had broken. Deference, deployed at the right moment, is leadership.

cites.quote: Whither shall I go to obtain food

spans.text: Whither shall I go to obtain food

phrases.term: According to the faith and diligence and heed
phrases.text: The pointers' operating conditions, stated as law: three inputs, all interior. The instrument is a gauge of its holders (Alma will draw the moral for his son centuries later, Alma 37:40), and the phrase warns every reader that guidance systems fail at the user's end.

phrases.term: A new writing, which was plain to be read
phrases.text: Revelation that updates: text "written and changed from time to time" (v. 29), always plain. The record's favorite quality (plainness) appears on heaven's own instrument panel, and the changing writing makes the Liahona the record's picture of living guidance: fixed in principle, current in instruction.

cites.quote: written and changed from time to time

spans.text: written and changed from time to time

verses.label: v. 1–5
verses.title: Hard words, soft landing
verses.text: The brothers protest "hard things, more than we are able to bear" (v. 1); Nephi answers with the proverb and an exhortation, and the scene ends in humbling and in his own durable optimism: "I had joy and great hopes of them" (v. 5). The record keeps Nephi's hope for his brothers alive long past the point where a reader might have retired it.

cites.quote: hard things, more than we are able to bear

spans.text: hard things, more than we are able to bear

cites.quote: I had joy and great hopes of them

spans.text: I had joy and great hopes of them

verses.label: v. 7–8
verses.title: Five weddings, one sentence of ink
verses.text: Nephi, his brothers, and Zoram marry the daughters of Ishmael, and the record spends no scene on it, only the note that the commandments were "fulfilled" (v. 8). The colony is complete: records, families, and now the marriages the errand of chapter 7 existed to make possible.

cites.quote: fulfilled

spans.text: fulfilled

verses.label: v. 9–12
verses.title: Command by night, compass by morning
verses.text: The record fixes the order of the two events by time of day: the command comes "by night" at verse 9, and the object is found in the morning "upon the ground" at the tent door. It is described in physical terms, "a round ball of curious workmanship; and it was of fine brass," with "two spindles" inside. The record gives the material, the shape, and the mechanism before it gives any interpretation, and the only function stated here is directional, that one spindle "pointed the way whither we should go." Alma 37:38 supplies the name Liahona and a translation, "which is, being interpreted, a compass," four hundred years later in the record's own chronology.

verses.label: v. 18–22
verses.title: The broken bow breaks the camp
verses.text: One snapped weapon, and hunger does what Laban's sword could not: everyone murmurs, "also my father began to murmur against the Lord his God" (v. 20). The record's honesty reaches its high-water mark: even the visionary head of the family has a breaking point, and it is supper.

cites.quote: also my father began to murmur against the Lord his God

spans.text: also my father began to murmur against the Lord his God

verses.label: v. 23–27
verses.title: A bow, a question, a chastening
verses.text: The record supplies the inventory before the question: "out of wood a bow, and out of a straight stick, an arrow," plus "a sling and with stones." Four items, three of them replacements for the steel bow broken at verse 18. Verse 25 then records that the answer came with a rebuke attached to the man who asked, and verse 27 records the reaction of everyone present, "he did fear and tremble exceedingly, and also my brethren and the sons of Ishmael and our wives." Verses 28 and 29 state the operating rule twice, that the pointers worked "according to the faith and diligence and heed which we did give unto them" and that the writing "was written and changed from time to time, according to the faith and diligence which we gave unto it."

verses.label: v. 28–32
verses.title: The pointers' law, and supper
verses.text: The spindles work "according to the faith and diligence and heed which we did give unto them" (v. 28); the chapter states the mechanics, then shows them: Nephi climbs where the ball says, kills food, and comes home to joy and thanksgiving. Small means, the record notes here for the first time in practice, do great things.

cites.quote: according to the faith and diligence and heed which we did give unto them

spans.text: according to the faith and diligence and heed which we did give unto them

verses.label: v. 34–39
verses.title: Nahom, grief, and a plot
verses.text: Ishmael dies; his daughters mourn and accuse; the old grievance resurfaces armed, "let us slay our father, and also our brother Nephi" (v. 37), with the ruler-and-teacher promise of 1 Nephi 2:22 now recited as evidence of ambition. The voice of the Lord itself ends the scene, and chastened anger cools into repentance once more.

cites.quote: let us slay our father, and also our brother Nephi

spans.text: let us slay our father, and also our brother Nephi

chapter.title: The wilderness cycle, run twice
chapter.text: Blessing, crisis, murmur, humbling, guidance, deliverance: the chapter runs the loop at the broken bow and again at Nahom. This is the journey's working rhythm, and the record sets it early so the reader can count the revolutions all the way to the sea.

chapter.title: Even the prophet murmurs
chapter.text: Verse 20 is the record's costliest honesty: Lehi, keeper of visions, breaks at hunger like everyone else, and is restored by the same mechanics he taught: inquiry, chastening, trembling obedience. No one in this record stands above its doctrine, which is why the doctrine can be trusted.

chapter.title: Guidance is a gauge
chapter.text: The Liahona's law (v. 28–29) makes direction a function of the travelers' interior state: faith, diligence, heed in; bearings out. The record's picture of revelation is an instrument that reads its reader, and its stillness is information.

chapter.title: Nephi leads by restoring his father
chapter.text: The bow-maker asks "whither shall I go?" of the man who just murmured. The move is the chapter's finest: competence without deference could have finished what the famine started, and Nephi spends his moment of maximum advantage re-dignifying the humbled head of the family.

chapter.title: The old grievance finds new fuel
chapter.text: The murder plot recites 1 Nephi 2:22 back as accusation, with ruler and teacher reframed as a brother's ambition, and dismisses angels as "his cunning arts" (v. 38). Unbelief, as the record draws it, is never a lack of data; it is an interpretive machine that can digest any miracle into a trick.

cites.quote: his cunning arts

spans.text: his cunning arts

chapter.title: The waypoints are checkable geography
chapter.text: Verse 13 supplies a duration, a bearing, and a place name in one sentence, "we traveled for the space of four days, nearly a south-southeast direction... and we did call the name of the place Shazer." Verse 33 keeps the same course, and verse 34 gives a second name, "buried in the place which was called Nahom." The record distinguishes the two: Shazer is a name the party gave, Nahom a name the place already had. A journey narrative that commits to bearings and distances can be checked against country in a way that a doctrinal claim cannot.

chapter.title: The voyage unit opens
chapter.text: Chapters 16–18 form the journey's arc, and this chapter supplies its terms: the instrument, the cycle, the family's fault lines. The escalations to come (the ship, the storm, the binding) will all run on machinery this chapter installed.

applications.title: Read the cut before blaming the blade
applications.text: The next time a sermon, verse, or plain word from someone stings, run the proverb: what did the cut find? Guilt reads truth as attack; the wound it locates is the item for tonight's prayer.

applications.title: Check the three dials
applications.text: When guidance goes quiet, audit the inputs the pointers ran on (faith, diligence, heed) one at a time, honestly. The instrument panel of your life is probably not broken; it is reading you.

applications.title: Fix what you can, then ask whither
applications.text: Nephi's crisis protocol: build the bow yourself, and route the direction through the order God established: parent, leader, covenant channels. Initiative and deference are not rivals; deployed together they rebuilt a family on the spot.

applications.title: Expect fertile parts
applications.text: Pray for and watch for the better path through your wilderness. Being led, in this chapter, means the hard country gets navigable, and learning to call that guidance is half of gratitude.

applications.title: Take your chastening like Lehi
applications.text: When correction comes (from the Lord, from circumstances, from the writing on whatever ball you carry) inquire, feel it, and adjust in front of your family. The record's greatest man modeled being wrong well, once, so the rest of us would know how.

applications.title: Give grief a place-name
applications.text: Let mourning have its Nahom: a real place, a real pause, real tears. And watch the turn the record warns of: grief that is not allowed to be grief will hire itself out to accusation.

questions.text: Which recent truth did I take to be hard, and what exactly did it cut?
Do I mark covenant milestones (marriages, callings, commandments fulfilled), or do they pass in one unnoticed verse?
What is my broken-bow scenario, the loss that would find out my murmuring point, and has it already happened without my noticing?
Whom should I be asking "whither shall I go," and whom have I been bypassing because I currently hold the working bow?
When did I last receive new writing, current and plain instruction for my situation, and what was I doing differently then?
Which of God's appointments in my life am I re-litigating as somebody's ambition?
